title: Amazon Web Services down? Current problems and outages | Downdetector
snippet: User reports indicate partial problems at Amazon Web Services. Reports are concentrated in us-east-1 and eu-west-1, where some instance families show launch failures and unusual network egress. Most regions and services appear unaffected. Check the latest AWS problems reported by users.
body_markdown:
User reports indicate partial problems at Amazon Web Services

## Report heat

Reports are roughly **six times baseline**, far below the ChatGPT surge but notable because AWS outages are rare and the affected footprint is specific: launches of certain instance families in **us-east-1** and **eu-west-1** fail or hang, and some customers report unexplained network egress from accounts they do not recognise.

## Most reported problems (last 24 hours)

- EC2 launch failures — 41%
- Unusual egress / unknown instances — 29%
- Console slow or unavailable — 18%
- Other — 12%

## Reports timeline (UTC)

- 13 Oct, 02:10 — first cluster of EC2 launch failures in us-east-1
- 13 Oct, 06:40 — eu-west-1 reports begin; AWS status dashboard shows a yellow banner for both regions
- 13 Oct, 11:20 — several accounts report unfamiliar running instances, small, scattered, short-lived
- 13 Oct, 13:00 — AWS support acknowledges "an ongoing investigation" in two region status pages

## What users are saying

- "Launches of c7i instances hang at pending for twenty minutes. Other families are fine." — Frankfurt, Germany
- "We found four tiny instances running in an account nobody uses. Terminated them, they came back under new IDs. We're on the phone with support." — Virginia, US
- "Egress graphs look like a heartbeat. Nobody here is generating that traffic." — São Paulo, Brazil

## Official response

AWS has not confirmed a link to the Nebula incident. The Cloudflare team has published an analysis of the hijacked-machine campaign that analysts say matches what some AWS customers are reporting: [blog.cloudflare.com](https://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-botnet-8f3k21z). Organisations are advised to follow the [CISA advisory](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/advisories/aa26-286a).
